popCulture.title: Rod of Asclepius
popCulture.description: A single serpent coiled on a staff remains medicine's true emblem — Asclepius' rod on ambulances, hospitals and the WHO seal, distinct from Hermes' twin-snake caduceus.

popCulture.title: Ophiuchus
popCulture.description: The serpent-bearer constellation is often read as Asclepius among the stars — the healer who learned from snakes, written across the summer Milky Way.

popCulture.title: Caduceus as a symbol of medicine
popCulture.description: Modern English still muddles Asclepius' rod with Hermes' caduceus — a standing reminder that the god of medicine and the god of merchants got crossed in print.
